description:
FOUND s492 (Fable, 2026-09-20) by the modules-work battery (#1994, mw-24).  Probes: ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/probes/open2a.pl, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s492/modwork/mw-24-IPC-Open2-Open3.pl.  Both modules LOAD (the s491 table counted them as working).  The shell error says a LIST-form exec is being flattened into ONE shell string somewhere on the path IPC::Open3's `_open3` takes: it forks and then `exec @_` / `exec { $_[0] } @_` with the handles dup'ed via `open(STDIN, "<&=" . fileno ...)` -- cheap discriminating measurement (not taken): under ./runpcl, `if (!fork) { exec("tr", "a-z", "A-Z") }` with STDIN redirected from a pipe -- does LIST-form `exec` reach execvp without a shell?  and `exec { "tr" } "tr", "a-z", "A-Z"` (the indirect-object form IPC::Open3 uses)?  If `exec LIST` is right alone, instrument a copy of IPC/Open3.pm as was done for File::Find (#2080's method).  perl's rule: `exec LIST` with more than one element NEVER goes through the shell; `system LIST` likewise (the battery's system("sh", "-c", "exit 3") IS right today).  ACCEPTANCE: mw-24 == perl (stdout of the child through open2; stdout+stderr+exit status through open3 with a gensym'd error handle).  BAR: `cl/` => full sweep + companion io/ op/exec.t legs, guard rows in an existing exec/pipe Pl/t file.

=== MEASURED s501 (Fable, 2026-09-30, ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/review/r501b-exec.pl; perl and main 77212b1f outputs in out/) ===
The family on main, row by row (everything else in the 20-row probe is right, incl. a LITERAL list `system("echo", "1", "a;b")`, fork + `exec("echo", ...)`, list-form pipe opens, backticks):
  rows 7 8   `my @cmd = ("echo", "7", "from array;x"); system(@cmd)` -> `/bin/sh: Syntax error: word unexpected (expecting ")")`, rc 2: an ARRAY argument reaches the shell as ONE string (the one-element array form, which perl DOES hand to the shell, fails the same way).  `system(@cmd) == 0 or die` is the commonest spelling in real scripts -- this is the row that matters most.
  rows 4 11  the indirect-object form `system { "sh" } "custom", "-c", ...` / `exec { "sh" } ...`: the first LIST element is run as the program (`sh: 0: cannot open custom`); perl runs the BLOCK`s program with the list as argv (argv[0] = "custom").
  rows 19 20 open2 / open3: `open(GLOB, "<&=", 4) failed: Bad file descriptor` -- the fd-ALIAS form of open (`<&=N`, `>&=N`) on a descriptor number, then the list command through the shell as above.
  row 6      a failed `system("/nonexistent", "a")` answers -1 and sets $! as perl does but prints no `Can`t exec ...` warning (cosmetic; #221 family).


=== DONE (s501b) ===
Shipped in the s501b batch (worktree agent-a8afc5670788453d5; commits "WIP s501b m1 (#2082)" + the review-round commit).  Four runtime gaps on IPC::Open2/Open3's one path, each probed vs perl 5.40.3:
  1. exec/system share ONE argument reading, `%p-command-words`: the args FLATTEN (`exec @_`, `system(@cmd)`); a LIST of >1 element never goes through a shell; ONE string goes to /bin/sh only by perl's do_exec3 rule (`%p-shell-command-p`: leading `. `/`exec `, `=` in the first word, a shell metachar or newline), else split on whitespace and execvp'd; `exec { PROG } LIST` / `system { PROG } LIST` are emitted `(p-exec :program PROG LIST…)` (PExpr marks the funcall `indirect_program`) and never use the shell.  The LIST after `{ PROG }` ends at a same-level `or` (`_take_rest_as_args`; `exec { "sh" } … or die` used to hand `die` to the program).
  2. `open FH, MODE, LIST` flattens its LIST (`%p-open-spread-args`) -- IPC::Open3's `open $_[0], $_[1], @_[2..$#_]`.
  3. `\*STDIN` / `*STDOUT` / `*STDERR` in a non-main package are `*main::…` (ExprToCL gen_symbol_form via `fh_forced_main_name`).
  4. `pipe` installs both ends through `%p-install-fh` (FD_CLOEXEC above $^F, a glob target), and the EMULATED exec (`%p-exec-spawn` + `%p-exec-become`) closes every descriptor before it waits; non-CLOEXEC fds go to the program (`:preserve-fds`).
Acceptance: mw-24 == perl; review probe r501b-exec == perl except rows 4 and 11 (argv[0]; not-supported.md "`exec { PROG } LIST` cannot set argv[0]; an emulated `exec` keeps a parent") and row 6's warnings-gated `Can't exec` line (#221).  Everyday modules/IPC-Open2-Open3 left the baseline.
Guards: Pl/t/system-block-01.t rows 1-2,4-5 (stale expectations rewritten to perl's output) + 38-45; 12 fail on the a0899ba6 code.  Companion A/B (--jobs 1, a0899ba6 extraction): io/openpid.t 8/2 -> OK 10/0 (UP), op/fork.t case pipe_to_fork fixed, op/sigsystem.t OK 4/0 -> 2/2 = two accidental passes made honest (the file's list constant returns its last element, #2537; perl's `system("exit 0")` is -1); both spliced by edit.  ir-spec §7.5b (normative).
Filed from this member: #2555 (system/qx do not inherit STDIN).
subject: BROKEN (everyday IPC): IPC::Open2 / IPC::Open3 with a LIST command fail -- `open2(my $out, my $in, "tr", "a-z", "A-Z")` prints "/bin/sh: 1: Syntax error: word unexpected (expecting ")")" and yields nothing; `open3(...)` with "sh", "-c", "..." likewise (rc=2 where perl has rc=4 and both output streams)
